correctness.rationale: Deuring–Shafarevich gives exactly two poles for p-rank 2, and Riemann–Hurwitz forces jumps summing to 5, hence the unordered pair (1,4). Moving poles to 0,∞ and Artin–Schreier reduction yields the stated normal form. Different exponents 4 and 10 and ramified orders v_0(x,y,dx)=(3,-1,4), v_∞(x,y,dx)=(-3,-4,4) yield five regular differential monomials dx/x,dx,x dx,y dx/x,y dx (and genus 5 establishes completeness). Semilinear Cartier gives C(e1)=e1, C(e4)=e4, C(e2)=C(e3)=0, C(e5)= -D^(1/3)e1-B^(1/3)e2; rank is 2 or 3, a=5-rank is 3 or 2 and C^2 has rank2. The cited rational index-three subfield uniqueness theorem in genus5,p-rank2 (not an exception) forces all automorphisms to preserve the x projection. Distinct pole jumps force x↦λx, comparison of x^-1 and x^4 gives λ^-1=u=λ^4 with u=±1; hence u=λ=1 and remaining deck y translations form C3. Independent mod-three Cartier-column enumeration covered all 36 F3 choices A,D≠0,B,C arbitrary and reproduced exact ranks and prime-field examples; the entire algebraically closed-field result relies on the abstract Cartier calculation and uniqueness theorem.
